Planet is a global company with employees working remotely world wide and joining us from offices in San Francisco, Washington DC, Germany, Austria, Slovenia, and The Netherlands. About the Role: In a dynamic international trade environment, compliance is the key to sustainable success. As a Working Student (m/f/d) in Export Control/ International Trade Compliance, you will actively support our International Trade Compliance team in the operational implementation, monitoring, and continuous improvement of our global export control processes. You will apply your theoretical knowledge directly to complex cases involving German, European, and US export regulations (EAR/ITAR). In this role, your work is the vanguard of our integrity. By rigorously enforcing export controls, managing licenses, and conducting thorough due diligence, you ensure that our advanced satellite technologies and sensitive data do not fall into the wrong hands. Your daily vigilance directly upholds Planet’s core values of global transparency, ethical business practices, and global security—allowing us to continue democratizing access to space while remaining a trusted, responsible partner on the global stage. Because compliance touches every aspect of our global operations, this role acts as a central hub. On a day-to-day basis, you will collaborate closely with: Product Managers & Engineering, Sales & Go-to-Market Teams, Logistics & Supply Chain, Purchasing/ Procurement, Internal IT & Operations, Physical Security & Lab Management. This is a temporary, part-time position and is expected to last 12 months. This hybrid position will require you to work from our Berlin office approx. 2 days per week. Impact You’ll Own: Classification & Screening: Assist in determining and assigning export control classification numbers (ECCN, national list numbers) as well as conducting systemic sanction list screenings, with Product Manager. Licensing Processes: Conduct preliminary checks of licensing requirements (BAFA, EU regulations) and US re-export regulations (EAR / ITAR) and support with preparation of license applications and license management, as needed. Documentation: Ensure transparent and audit-proof documentation of decision-making processes and audit trails. Contract Review: Review and evaluate export control-relevant clauses in customer and supplier agreements. Legal Monitoring: Monitor legal changes in national and international foreign trade law and prepare their implications for day-to-day business operations. Processes & IT: Support process modeling, identify optimization potential, and coordinate interfaces with internal IT systems (e.g., ERP/NetSuite/Oracle). Communication: Act as a central link and point of contact for internal departments such as Sales, Purchasing, Logistics, and IT. AccessControls Lab/ Visitor Requests: Evaluate and approve visitor requests and laboratory access permissions to mitigate deemed export risks, ensuring compliance with physical security protocols and technology transfer controls in sensitive areas. Review international Shipments: Perform export compliance reviews and release holds on international outbound shipments, verifying end-use, licensing coverage, and documentation prior to dispatch. Anti-Bribery/KYC/DueDiligence: Conduct risk-based third-party due diligence and Know-Your-Customer (KYC) assessments on business partners, evaluating red flags and enforcing adherence to anti-bribery and anti-corruption (ABAC) policies. What You Bring: Actively enrolled in an accredited university program in Business Law (LL.B.), International Trade, Logistics/Supply Chain Management with a focus on Customs, or a comparable degree program. Fluent written and spoken German and English (essential for navigating legal references). Interest in foreign trade issues, ideally paired with initial exposure to EU Dual Use Regulation or US export control regulations like Export Administration Regulation (EAR)/ International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). Detail-oriented with solid analytical capabilities; equipped with the ability to pragmatically translate complex legal texts into actionable corporate workflows. Proficiency in Google Office Application; familiarity with ERP systems or process modeling tools is an advantage. Application Deadline: 11:45p / 23:45 CET on the date stated below. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. This posting may be removed earlier than projected if a suitable pool of applications has been received. For this reason, we recommend applying as soon as you are able to. This position requires access to U.S. and German/EU export-controlled information, and as such, employment (or hiring of a contractor) is contingent upon the candidate’s ability to access all applicable export-controlled information without additional export licensing being required by German, EU, or U.S. authorities.
